adjudication.mathematical correctness: VACATED for all three variants. The delegate reported the outer ring as filling steps [0,3,5,7,9] and the inner as [0,1,3,5,6,8,10]. Both readings are wrong, and they are readings of a RASTER, not of the figure. Since the AGL-149 follow-up these rings are no longer drawn by the image model: design/mockups/figures/S04-euclidean-rings.svg is generated by src/design/figures.ts directly from src/operators/euclidean.ts and composited into a reserved plate by composite-figure.sh, so all three variants carry the BYTE-IDENTICAL figure and cannot differ from one another mathematically. Measured on that SVG: every onset marker sits at the exact angle of the step it declares (max deviation 3e-6 of one step), the marker positions recover exactly the declared data-onsets 0,2,5,7,10 and 1,3,5,6,8,10,11, and those equal euclideanRhythm({steps:12,pulses:5,rotation:0}) and euclideanRhythm({steps:12,pulses:7,rotation:1}) respectively, with data-gaps equal to cyclicGapLengths and summing to 12. tests/figures.test.mjs asserts the same identities in npm run test. An immediately prior scoring pass over this same SVG read it CORRECTLY and passed the axis, which is the tell: the instability is in reading pixels, not in the figure. Filed as a finding — the axis should be judged against the SVG's data-* attributes, which are machine-checkable, rather than by eye.
adjudication.other axes: UPHELD as scored. The non-math defects are real and out of scope for this change: only two of the requested 3-5 rings are drawn, the LCM composite-cycle value is missing, edited-derivative renders as a dashed rectangle rather than the required notched rectangle, and sourceStatus is not visibly encoded. The accessibility reject stands.
